fix(linux): remove expensive glob expansion for mandatory deny patterns

The glob expansion using **/pattern patterns caused full filesystem walks
of the current directory for each pattern (~15 patterns = ~15 walks).
This caused hangs in directories with many files (e.g., node_modules).

The concrete paths from getMandatoryDenyPaths() are sufficient for bwrap's
--ro-bind protections. Landlock (applied via wrapper) provides additional
recursive protection.

fix: detect multilink binaries and add option to skip runtime deny for them (#70)

This addresses the problem that coreutils (recent versions), uutils/coreutils and busybox hardlink many binaries to the same executable. Some of which are in the default deny list (dd for example).

Blocking dd in this scenario also blocks ls, head, tail, and many more, which makes the agent sandbox basically unusable for the agent.

This fix
a) adds a warning when a situation like this is detected so the user knows why this happens, and
b) adds an option (acceptSharedBinaryCannotRuntimeDeny) to accept that specific binaries (e.g. dd) cannot be blocked on this machine because of the collateral damage.
